summary: Parkevtate Vosianc revisits Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) and asks whether it is still a buying opportunity or too late after a ~48% YTD run in 2026. The core thesis: Agentic AI is adding a new leg of demand on top of the existing accelerator/data-center boom — demand for CPUs, memory and storage that was less emphasized before — and TSM is already sold out, forcing a capacity ramp including an additional $100B Arizona investment. TTM revenue is ~$143B with the slope accelerating since ChatGPT; TTM operating margins hit a record 55.84% on high utilization and premium pricing. Risks: Arizona production costs are much higher than Taiwan and management has been guiding for declining margins (though that has not materialized for over a year), plus tariffs and geopolitical concentration. Capital allocation has been above WACC for roughly three decades, so he trusts the heavy capex. Valuation: forward P/E is near a two-year high but below the S&P 500 average — he attributes the discount entirely to the Taiwan geopolitical risk premium. His updated DCF puts fair value at $639 vs a $445 market price, ~43% upside over 12-18 months. He reiterates his Aug 31 BUY and upgrades conviction from medium to high. Mentions Nvidia, Apple, AMD as key customers, and previews a members-only live on Micron earnings Sep 30. Call: TSM — BUY @ $445 stated (DCF fair value $639).
